feedback.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{3{n}^{3}(2{n}^{2}+1)}{(4{n}^{3}-5)(4{n}^{3}+5)}$ for $n\ge 1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{3{n}^{3}(2{n}^{2}+1)}{(4{n}^{3}-5)(4{n}^{3}+5)}=\frac{6{n}^{5}+3{n}^{3}}{16{n}^{6}-25}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{6{n}^{5}+3{n}^{3}}{16{n}^{6}-25}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $16{n}^{6},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{6}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{6{n}^{5}+3{n}^{3}}{16{n}^{6}-25} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{6{n}^{5}}{{n}^{6}}+\frac{3{n}^{3}}{{n}^{6}})}{(\frac{16{n}^{6}}{{n}^{6}}-\frac{25}{{n}^{6}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{6}{n}+\frac{3}{{n}^{3}})}{(16-\frac{25}{{n}^{6}})} \\  & =\frac{0+0}{16-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $0.$
